title: On‑call & Incident Response Playbook — Standards, Runbooks, and Templates
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standard on-call and incident response process, runbook templates for common production incidents, on-call rotation rules, game day guidance, and customer communication templates for the status page and direct comms. It is intended for engineers, SREs, support, and customer success staff who participate in incident handling.

Goals:
- Restore customer-facing functionality quickly and safely.
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-repair while preserving data security.
- Provide clear escalation paths and ownership.
- Standardize post-incident review and continuous improvement.

Scope:
- Applies to all production services: hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane, and infra components that affect inference (GPU fleet, routers, gateways, and databases).
- Includes severity definitions, runbooks for priority incident classes, rotation rules, game day process, and templated communications.

1) Incident classification and severity
- Sev 1 (P0): Complete outage or data-loss impacting >20% customers or critical business workflows (e.g., inference API returning 5xx for most requests). Target response: acknowledge in 5 minutes, restore or mitigation in 60 minutes.
- Sev 2 (P1): Degraded service with major impact to latency, throughput, or failures affecting a subset of customers/features. Target response: acknowledge in 15 minutes, restore or mitigation in 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (P2): Functional degradation with limited customer impact (e.g., elevated error rate for a minor route). Target response: acknowledge in 1 business day, resolution in 5 business days or scheduled fix.
- Sev 4 (P3): Non-urgent operational tasks, minor docs or metrics gaps.

2) Roles & responsibilities
- Pager (Primary on-call): First responder, triage, initial mitigation, and communication with team.
- Secondary (Escalation): Support pager after 15–30 minutes for Sev1 or when asked.
- Incident Commander (IC): Takes charge at declared incident (typically for Sev1/Sev2). Coordinates cross-functional efforts, decisions, and external comms.
- Scribe/Communications: Writes timeline, internal Slack updates, and customer-facing status page entries.
- Engineering Owner: Service owner responsible for root cause identification and remediation plan.
- Postmortem Author: Typically the incident owner or IC; documents timeline, root cause, actions.

3) Detection & Triage checklist (first 15 minutes)
1. Acknowledge PagerDuty alert and join #incidents Slack channel.
2. Triage: Confirm scope (services, regions, customers), collect key metrics: error rate, latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth.
3. Assign roles: Pager, Secondary, IC (if applicable), Scribe.
4. If Sev1: open incident in Incident Tracker (confluence incident page template), update status page with "investigating" and send initial customer-facing note (template below).
5. Apply fast mitigations (traffic routing, scale up, feature toggle, rollback).

4) Runbook templates (use these as step-by-step guides)
A. GPU node OOM / out-of-memory on serving nodes (common cause: sudden request spikes or memory leak)
- Detect: Elevated OOM/killed processes in node logs; increased OOM events in metrics; increased 5xx errors.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Isolate affected hosts: remove from load balancer (kube cordon/drain or fleet router remove).
  2) Check model versions recently rolled out (last 60 minutes). If a canary rollout occurred, rollback canary first.
  3) Restart serving processes and inspect core dumps/logs.
  4) If memory leak suspected: scale up horizontal replicas with conservative batch sizes and enable KV cache bypass for suspect models.
- Escalation: If >20% capacity impacted or repeated restarts, declare Sev1 and notify IC.
- Post-incident: Collect heap profiles / coredump, create CI test to reproduce and add regression guardrail.

B. High tail latency on hosted API (routing / autoscale / caching regression)
- Detect: P50 within SLO but P99 elevated > 500ms above target; customer complaints for slow responses.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Check routing policies, identify if traffic shifted to higher-latency pool (region/variant).
 2) Inspect batch sizes and batching backlog; reduce maximum batching window to prioritize latency.
 3) Disable non-critical middleware (observability hooks, expensive rerankers) for affected routes.
  4) Add capacity in Dedicated pools or move traffic to warmed hosts.
- Escalation: If customers experience >25% requests at high latency, raise to Sev1/Sev2 depending on scope.
- Post-incident: Tune autoscaler thresholds and add synthetic tests for P99 across representative prompt sets.

C. Authentication/Authorization outage (token service, KMS, or IAM integration)
- Detect: 401/403 errors across multiple services, failed calls to KMS, or a broken OIDC provider.
- Immediate actions:
  1) Validate token service health, check KMS logs, and confirm provider status (cloud provider status pages).
 2) If KMS is impacted and we have fallback wrapped keys, switch to fallback policy (documented key version).
 3) For external IDP outages, use emergency service account tokens as prescribed in secure emergency access runbook (requires approval).
- Escalation: Declare Sev1 if majority of requests fail auth checks. Notify security and legal if keys or credentials were compromised.
- Post-incident: Rotate affected keys, update secrets rotation policy if needed, and perform security review.

5) Escalation policy and timelines
- Pager escalates to Secondary after 15 minutes for Sev1, 30 minutes for Sev2.
- If IC not yet assigned after 20 minutes on a Sev1, Pager must call SRE lead and request immediate IC assignment.
- Executive notifications: For Sev1 incidents with customer impact >24 hours or potential legal/regulatory impact, inform Head of Ops and Legal.

6) Communication templates
- Status page (initial investigating):
  Title: "Investigating: Degraded API responses in us-west1"
  Body: "We are investigating an issue affecting inference responses for a subset of requests in us-west1. Customers may see increased errors or latency. Our engineers are actively triaging. We will post updates every 30 minutes or sooner."

- Status page (mitigated):
  Title: "Mitigated: Routing change restored capacity in us-west1"
  Body: "A routing configuration change reduced error rate and latency for affected requests. We are monitoring and will follow up with a detailed postmortem."

- Customer email (initial):
  Subject: "Redwood Inference — Investigating service degradation"
  Body: "Hello,

We are currently investigating an issue causing degraded inference performance for customers in <region>. You may observe increased latency or errors. We are actively working on mitigation and will send updates via status.redwood.ai and direct email. Estimated next update: <time>.

If you need immediate assistance or have a critical SLA concern, reply to this message and our support team will escalate.

— Redwood Inference Support"

- Customer email (post-mitigation):
  Subject: "Service update: Issue mitigated — follow-up and next steps"
  Body: "Hello,

The issue impacting inference in <region> has been mitigated by <short description of mitigation>. We are continuing to monitor. A postmortem will be published at <link> once RCA and follow-up actions are complete.

If you observed data loss or other persistent issues, please reply to this message.

— Redwood Inference Support"

7) On-call rotations and staffing rules
- Rotation length: 1 week per engineer for primary Pager.
- Secondary coverage: two-week rotations, overlaps by two days with primary for handoff.
- Handoffs: Before rotation change, outgoing on-call must post a handoff message in #oncall-handoffs summarizing ongoing incidents, alerts, and recent changes.
- Eligibility: Engineers must have completed on-call runbook training and at least one shadow week.
- Time-off: If a scheduled on-call cannot cover a rotation, they must swap using the on-call schedule tool and inform SRE manager 72 hours in advance.

8) Game days and continuous verification
- Cadence: Quarterly game days conducted by Eng SRE with participation from Platform, Serving Runtime, and Customer Success.
- Objectives: Validate runbooks, verify escalations, test failover between regions, and exercise communications.
- Format: Pre-brief (30m), scenario execution (60–90m), and retro & action tracking (60m). All game day scenarios must create at least one follow-up ticket with owner and target date.

9) Postmortem process and required artifacts
- Postmortem timeline: Draft within 72 hours of incident mitigation; review with reviewers within 7 days; publish final within 14 days.
- Required contents:
  - Incident summary and timeline (UTC timestamps)
  - Impacted customers and services
  - Root cause analysis & contributing factors
  - Mitigations taken and why they worked/didn't
  - Action items (owner + target date) with severity classification (short/medium/long-term)
  - Test plan for verifying closures and regression prevention
  - Link to logs, traces, and artifacts (where allowed)

10) Metrics, SLOs, and dashboards used for decisioning
- Key dashboards: API error-rate overview, routing and pool health, GPU utilization, model latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99), authentication success rate, and queue/backlog metrics.
- SLOs (examples):
  - API availability: 99.95% monthly uptime for core text generation routes.
  - P99 latency: <600ms for interactive generation (documented per model class).
  - Embeddings latency: P95 <200ms for standard regions.
- Alerts: Configure alerts on SLO burn rate (4x burn within 1 hour), absolute thresholds (error rate >1% sustained 5m), and resource saturation (GPU memory >85% for >10m).

11) Tools, links, and runbook references
- PagerDuty: Redwood Production (primary) & Redwood Staging (secondary) — escalation policies configured per-service.
- Slack channels: #incidents (IC and Scribe), #oncall-handoffs, #ops-escalations (exec notifications).
- Incident tracker template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-template (use when opening an incident page).
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai (edit by Communications role or IC).

12) Continuous improvement and governance
- Each postmortem must track action item closure and verification tests. Unresolved Sev1 actions older than 30 days will be escalated to Head of Ops.
- The playbook is reviewed quarterly by Eng SRE and updated after every game day.

Appendices:
A) Quick checklist (for first responder)
- Acknowledge alert and join #incidents
- Post initial status page message if impact affects customers
- Cull useful logs/traces and attach to incident page
- Identify mitigation and apply traffic or capacity changes
- Escalate per policy and assign IC if needed

B) Incident page template (use in Confluence)
- Title: [INCIDENT] YYYY-MM-DD — <short description>
- Fields: Severity, Start time, End time, IC, Scribe, Impacted services, Customers affected, Summary, Timeline, Root cause, Actions, Links

C) Customer comms checklist
- Keep tone factual and empathetic
- Include impact, mitigation steps, ETA for next update, and link to postmortem when available
- Avoid technical speculation in initial messages

If you are on-call and uncertain about next steps, escalate early to your Secondary or SRE lead. This playbook is the canonical internal doc — link to it from any service-specific runbook and keep service owners listed on the incident page.
